book.title: Traction: Get a Grip on Your Business
book.author: Gino Wickman

confidence_note: Book not read; vision pieces and Image One from a summary; EOS terms. Year omitted. Growth figure and 'one page' claim omitted.
facts: Six components: vision, people, data, issues, process, traction.
Vision: three to seven core values, a core focus, ten-year target, three-year picture, one-year plan, quarterly Rocks, a target market.
Three-year picture and one-year plan carry revenue, profit and measurables.
Image One dropped its networking division to return to simplifying clients' printing.
Rocks: 10-20 goals narrowed to about seven, each with one owner; 1-3 personal Rocks per leader; 90 days is about the limit of focus on one project.
scene_details: seven Rocks each with one name
a ladder from ten years to one quarter
tension: Vision stays in the founder's head.

lessons.idea: Tie the far goal to one job this quarter.

reflect_final: Which single job could you finish in three months and give to one person?

use_cases.situation: Too many priorities for the quarter
use_cases.move: Cut to about seven and give each an owner.

use_cases.situation: Employee can't say what their goal feeds
use_cases.move: Which yearly goal does your work feed? Pick one job.
That company dropped networking to return to printing. What would I drop?

pocket_idea: Bring the ten-year target down to this quarter: choose the job with one name next to it.

conversation_variants.punchline_idea: A vision is real when it lands as one job on one desk.
